## Context Pull request 51 adopts the SDK's `scanMutationSecrets` for memory writes and imports. In seven review rounds, every round found one more spelling that slips past the scan when a credential sits inside mixed content: - a quoted key (`"password":"…"`, `'password':'…'`); - a value nested in an array or object (`Config: {"password":["…"]}`, `{"password":{"value":"…"}}`); - a reference suffix, an unterminated quote, or bracket quoting. Each fix added another case to a local parser. The SDK has the same gap: `scanMutationSecrets` on 2026.11.10 returns no finding for any quoted-key form, even a flat `{"password":"…"}`, while it flags `password: …`. This is filed upstream as unbraind/pm-cli issue 1699. ## Decision Pull request 51 merges at its real scope: SDK transaction readers, revision guards, and the scan for unquoted assignments, reference suffixes and quoted values. Its tests cover those forms. The structural quoted-key and nested-value class is handled here instead of in more per-round patches. ## Work 1. When pm-cli issue 1699 ships, raise the `@unbrained/pm-cli` peer floor to that release. Delete the local mixed-content handling that the SDK rule then covers, and keep only what is still memory-specific. 2. Add a must-refuse corpus with the quoted-key, nested-array, nested-object and XML forms above, and a must-allow corpus (`"password": ""`, `"password": "${BUILD_PASSWORD}"`, `"password_policy": "rotate monthly"`, prose that mentions a password field). Run both through `remember`, `import` and portable transfer. 3. Until then, the README's security section states which forms are not yet refused. ## Acceptance - Both corpora pass through every write path, and each must-refuse case fails when the scan is reverted. - No local regex duplicates an SDK rule. --- ### GitHub comments (3) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-10T12:02:16Z) > > > > > >

Drop into our [discord](https://discord.gg/coderabbit)! > **@unbraind** (2026-11-10T17:18:26Z) > > Another must-refuse case for the corpus, found by the review of the final round of pull request 51 (head 717b584): environment-reference masking accepts a literal concatenated after an empty reference. In `password=${EMPTY}"SyntheticOnly123!"`, the quoted literal becomes the password when EMPTY is empty, yet the scan masks the whole value as a reference and admits it. Same class as the quoted-key and nested-value forms: deciding what counts as a reference belongs in the shared SDK rule, not a local parser. The corpus should also cover `${VAR}literal`, `$VAR"literal"` and `literal${VAR}` as must-refuse, and `${VAR}` alone as must-allow. > **@unbraind** (2026-11-10T17:55:45Z) > > Upstream status: unbraind/pm-cli pull request 1701 (for issue 1699) adds SDK recognition of quoted keys, values nested in arrays and objects, escaped literals and `` elements. The env-reference concatenation case (`password=${EMPTY}"literal"`, `$VAR"literal"`, `literal${VAR}`) is not in it. It is tracked upstream as pm-cli item pm-ycgb5g, because fixing it changes the flat value grammar that also drives the repository scan. Plan: raise the peer floor and delete the local quoted/nested parsing when 1701 ships, and keep the env-reference must-refuse cases as known gaps until pm-ycgb5g ships.
